chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Salman (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'The soul tends to disturb its owner when there does not happen to be the livelihood for it what can be relied upon. So when its livelihood is kept aside, it feels secure'.
ai.seo_question: How does securing livelihood affect the peace of the soul according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the psychological impact of economic instability, illustrating how the soul's agitation (iltiath) is directly tied to the uncertainty of daily sustenance. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that material security is a prerequisite for spiritual tranquility, linking the preservation of foodstuffs to the preservation of inner peace.
